summary: An excerpt from a novel (Book 12, part 68) in which Lexy meets a naval officer on the road near Wyngate, and they talk about his romance with Caroline. He explains they met a year earlier aboard the Ormond, corresponded through a servant named Annie, and planned to marry despite the Enderbys' disapproval of his lack of money. Lexy is moved and sympathetic, and the conversation shows her learning the full story while he gets emotional about Caroline's family and his situation.
one_line: Lexy meets a naval officer near Wyngate who reveals his secret correspondence and planned marriage with Caroline.
key_facts: Lexy and the officer walk back toward Mrs. Royce's house in Wyngate after meeting on the road.
The officer's ship's engines broke down in bad weather and it returned to port for repairs.
He obtained leave from the old man (his commanding officer) for what he called very important business.
Mrs. Royce told him Lexy had gone out to the Queltons'.
He met Caroline about a year earlier on board the Ormond, when she and her parents were seasick most of the time.
A servant girl named Annie posted Caroline's letters for her, and he wrote to Caroline in care of Annie's mother.
Caroline's family did not approve of him; he says he would not have suited them.
He says he has no money beyond his pay, but that it was enough for the two of them to live on.
He asked Caroline to marry him, telling her they could have had a jolly sort of life.
Caroline said she would meet him in Wyngate, the nearest main-line station to a little place where a nurse or governess of hers lived.
Lexy says she has never heard of the governess's name, Miss Craigie, when it is mentioned.
Lexy admits she is crying a little, and says she is awfully sorry for him.
